title: Kernel ladderized eviction and compact allocator for paged KV
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Reduce tail prefill/decode latency and KV thrashing by introducing a two-part runtime: (1) a ladderized eviction scorer that ranks fragments by age, stride-impact, and kernel-compatibility; and (2) a compact-allocator that opportunistically merges small adjacent fragments to reduce fragmentation and improve kernel throughput. This ticket covers design, implementation, benchmarks, and rollout gating for the ladderized eviction + compact allocator on paged attention KV caches.

Background: Current paged-KV allocation favors simple LRU-like heuristics which lead to frequent small-fragment eviction and re-prefill cycles for long-lived sequences. That increases prefill work and causes suboptimal kernel selection because kernels prefer contiguous, compact memory for high throughput. We need a scoring and allocation layer that is eviction-aware and kernel-aware simultaneously so we can: (a) stabilize residency for hot spans, (b) merge micro-fragments when cost-effective, and (c) steer kernel selection (fast/compact kernels vs. sparse kernels) based on expected residency and fragmentation.

Scope: Design eviction scoring, fragment merge policy, allocator API changes, scheduler hooks for prefill/decode admission, metrics + dashboards, unit/bench tests, canary rollout plan. Excludes cross-tenant shared reservoir refactor (tracked separately).
acceptance_criteria: Eviction scorer implemented and exposed as a pluggable policy in allocator
Compact-allocator merges fragments with low merge-cost and improves compactness metric by >= 20% in synthetic workloads
End-to-end 95th percentile prefill latency reduced by >= 15% on multi-tenant p95 workload compared to baseline
Kernel selector demonstrates measurable preference shift to compact kernels when compactness improves
Automated tests covering merge correctness, fragmentation invariants, and scorer stability
Canary rollout runbook and rollback hooks documented in Console (link in attachments)

implementation_notes:
High-level algorithm: compute eviction_score = w1*staleness + w2*decode_cost_est + w3*stride_penalty + w4*fragment_penalty - w5*kernel_compatibility_bonus. Runtime adjusts weights by occupancy and tenant class. Compact merge rule: merge two adjacent fragments if merge_cost_est < merge_benefit_threshold and resulting fragment size aligns with kernel block size. Admission: if allocator predicts merge will cause backpressure (> soft-reserve threshold), defer merge to background compaction window. Kernel selection: annotate fragments with kernel_compatibility_score and let scheduler prefer kernels with higher expected throughput for contiguous fragments.

Implementation milestones: prototype scorer and metadata (week 1), compact-allocator merge pass + tests (week 2), scheduler integration (week 3), canary + measurements (week 4).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Aggressive merging increases memory dwell and OOM risk for bursty workloads. Mitigation: conservative merge thresholds, tie to occupancy and soft-reserve, add background decanting window.
Risk: Kernel hint coupling may create oscillation between kernels. Mitigation: keep hints advisory, add hysteresis and kernel preference smoothing over minutes.
Risk: Cross-tenant fairness regressions. Mitigation: enforce tenant-weighted eviction credits and ensure soft-reserve per-tenant quotas are respected.
Risk: Increased CPU overhead for scoring and merge decision making. Mitigation: batch score updates, do merge decisions in background worker, approximate scoring for cold pages.
test_plan: Unit tests for scorer normalization and invariants
Property tests for merge correctness and fragmentation invariants
Microbench: single-tenant long-context workload, compare decode throughput and kernel profile distribution
Multi-tenant stress: measure prefill/re-prefill cycles and p95/p99 latencies
Canary: 48h run on dedicated pool, monitor metrics in Console and run automated rollback if p99 decode latency worsens by >10% or OOM incidents occur
notes: Prefer lightweight scoring implementations to keep hot-path allocation cheap. Will iterate on feature weights using reinforcement tuning from offline traces. If compact-allocator proves too risky in canary, fallback plan is to ship only eviction scorer and expose merge opt-in per-tenant.
